brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Evening edition. It covers the 24 hours to 17:10 CEST on 22 October; new research covers 05:10 CEST to 17:10 CEST on 22 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Ukraine's General Staff Reports Hits on Bryansk Jamming Station and Luhansk Depot
items.lede: Kyiv's military says destroying such jammers frees its drone units to operate, and it also listed two Russian command posts hit in Zaporizhzhia region.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck an electronic warfare station near Gulevka in Russia's Bryansk region, a logistics depot near Zolotarivka in occupied Luhansk region, and command posts near Vyshneve and Lankove in Zaporizhzhia region on 21 October and overnight [1]. It said knocking out jamming assets widens room for Ukrainian drone use [1]. No Russian comment and no independent imagery were found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low to moderate, because the claims come only from Ukraine's General Staff relayed by a state agency, with no independent check.

items.title: Russian Strike on Lozova Market Kills Two in Ukraine's Kharkiv Region
items.lede: Seventeen people were wounded at the market by midday, the governor said, a day after strikes across the region killed one and injured 15.

sections.text: A Russian strike on a market in Lozova, Kharkiv region, Ukraine, killed two people and injured 17 by midday on 22 October, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said [2]. On 21 October Russian attacks hit Kharkiv city and 11 settlements in the region, killing a 42-year-old woman in Lymanivka and injuring 15 people, three of them children, he said in his morning summary [3]. He listed two missiles, four Molniya drones, five FPV drones, and 120 other drones used against the region [3]. No Russian statement on the Lozova target was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the casualty figures, because they come on record from the regional governor in two releases. Confidence on what Russia aimed at is low, because no account of the target was found.

items.title: Russia Hands Ukraine 252 Bodies in Repatriation Ahead of Planned Talks
items.lede: Kyiv sent 25 bodies the other way, Belarusian state media said, as the Red Cross-assisted handover came a day after Moscow agreed in principle to resume talks.

sections.text: Russia returned the bodies of 252 people to Ukraine on 22 October, which the Russian side said were Ukrainian soldiers, Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War said, thanking the Red Cross for help [4]. Ukrainian investigators and forensic experts will identify the remains [4]. Reuters, citing Belarus's Belta agency, said Ukraine handed over 25 bodies in return, and noted such exchanges have accompanied moves toward talks before [5].

Confidence is high on the 252 bodies, because Ukraine's official body and Reuters agree. Confidence on the 25 bodies returned to Russia is moderate, because it rests on Belarusian state media relayed by Reuters.

items.title: Ukraine's Southern Command Says Russia Readies Autumn Armoured Push
items.lede: Huliaipole sees 10 to 20 clashes a day, a military spokesperson said, while strikes killed three people around Zaporizhzhia city over the past day.

sections.text: Anastasiia Shevchenko, deputy spokesperson for Ukraine's Operation Task Force South, said Russian forces had finished preparing mechanized autumn attacks after a months-long pause and were moving armour into launch areas [6]. She named the Huliaipole sector as the hottest, with 10 to 20 clashes a day, and said Russia now mostly uses infiltration and small groups on motorcycles and quad bikes [6]. Zaporizhzhia regional chief Ivan Fedorov said Russian strikes killed three people and injured three in and around Zaporizhzhia over the past day, with 862 strikes on 48 settlements [7]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the armour build-up, because it rests on one Ukrainian military spokesperson without outside confirmation. Confidence is high on the Zaporizhzhia toll, because it is an on-record official figure.

items.title: Russian Ballistic Missiles Kill One and Injure 22 in Kyiv Overnight
items.lede: Zelensky said three of the 21 missiles carried cluster warheads, one striking near the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra in the historic centre of Ukraine's capital.

sections.text: Russia fired at least 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv, Ukraine, in three waves from late on 21 October, Zelensky said [5]. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said strikes hit six districts, killing one person in Dniprovskyi and injuring 22, among them children; eight were hurt in Pecherskyi, where ambulances and a monastery were damaged, and a restaurant complex burned in Sviatoshynskyi [8]. The Kyiv Independent's first report put the injured at six [9], and transport infrastructure was damaged in Darnytskyi [8]. Zelensky said three missiles had cluster warheads that burst in the air over a 400-metre radius, one hitting between the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra and the Holy Vvedensky Monastery, and called the choice of weapon and target deliberate [10]. He mocked Witkoff's description of Putin as a humanitarian [5]. No Russian statement on the Kyiv targets was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the strike and the toll, because Ukrainian emergency services, the mayor, and Reuters agree. Confidence on the cluster-warhead detail is moderate, because it rests on Zelensky's account.

items.title: Moscow Mayor Says 630 Ukrainian Drones Targeted Russia's Capital Region Overnight
items.lede: Astra reported a blast and fire at the 75 Arsenal weapons plant in Serpukhov, while Moscow said 163 drones were stopped on the approach to the capital.

sections.text: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 630 drones flew toward the Moscow region between 19:30 CEST on 21 October and 03:00 CEST on 22 October, that most were destroyed far out, and that 163 were neutralised on the approach to the Russian capital [11]. He said two people were hurt in Moscow's Troitsky and Novomoskovsky districts [11]. Debris also damaged an apartment block in Lipetsk, injuring one person [11]. Russian authorities reported more than 160 drones heading for Moscow, AFP reported [12]. No Ukrainian statement on targets and no independent damage reporting were found by the cutoff. Drones hit the 75 Arsenal plant in Serpukhov, Moscow region, Russia, according to Astra, which cited eyewitness footage of an explosion and fire; the plant answers to Russia's Main Missile and Artillery Directorate [13]. Reuters said Russia reported 630 drones aimed at Moscow overnight [5]. No Russian Defence Ministry confirmation of damage at Serpukhov was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the figures come only from the Russian mayor, relayed by a Russian outlet and by AFP, with no independent check.

items.title: Kremlin Agrees in Principle to Resume Three-Way Talks after Putin Meets Witkoff
items.lede: Russia's Ushakov saw little substance in the European and Ukrainian ideas Witkoff carried, even as Trump called a settlement maybe the closest yet.

sections.text: Putin received US envoy Steve Witkoff at the Constantine Palace in St Petersburg, Russia, on 21 October for about three hours, a day after Witkoff's Oslo talks with Zelensky; Jared Kushner joined remotely [14][12]. Putin freed jailed American Stephen Hubbard, and Trump said no swap was needed [14][15]. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia was ready in principle to resume three-way talks in mid-November on postwar security, that the Oslo proposals lacked substance, and that a Putin, Trump, and Xi summit was being prepared in Shenzhen, China, for next month [16][12]. Witkoff called the talks constructive and said technical-level contacts would continue [12]. Trump said a deal was maybe the closest yet and defended delaying sanctions to free Hubbard [12]. Zelensky said Kyiv favours a meeting as soon as possible [12].

Confidence is high on the meeting, Hubbard's release, and the on-record remarks, because the Kremlin transcript and several outlets agree. Confidence on the talks timetable and the summit is moderate, because both rest on Ushakov's account.

items.title: Ukraine Counts About 60 Russian Strikes on Energy Sites Since 19 October
items.lede: State energy firms warned this winter may be among the hardest of the war and asked partners for faster air defence and repair money.

sections.text: Ukraine's Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said Russia has made around 60 targeted strikes on energy and oil and gas infrastructure since 19 October, including in Rivne, Volyn, Khmelnytskyi, and Vinnytsia regions [17]. He said the capital's combined heat and power plants had been damaged, and that available generation capacity was insufficient to keep the capital's energy hub resilient [17]. Naftogaz, Ukrenergo, Energoatom, the gas transmission operator, and Ukrhydroenergo jointly urged partners to speed air defence, repair funding, winter gas and power imports, and oil and gas sanctions, warning the winter could be among the hardest of the war [18]. No independent damage assessment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because both statements come from Ukrainian officials and state companies via one outlet.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Britain Proposes 14-Year Terms for Saboteurs of Undersea Cables and Pipelines
items.lede: London cites suspicious Russian activity near British waters and says it is replacing 140-year-old laws, with a 12-week public consultation starting now.

sections.text: The UK government published a White Paper on 22 October proposing new offences for intentional, reckless, or negligent damage to undersea telecoms and energy infrastructure, with prison terms of up to 14 years and unlimited fines for ship owners [1]. It would place security duties on subsea cable operators and let ministers direct them where national security is at risk [1]. Telecoms Minister Ian Murray cited suspicious Russian activity around undersea infrastructure, and the department recalled an April exposure of a covert Russian submarine operation near UK waters [1]. A 12-week consultation now opens [1].
Confidence is high on the proposals, because they come from the government's own release. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Ukraine Says Gerasimov Falsely Placed Russian Troops Five Kilometres From Zaporizhzhia
items.lede: Kyiv's southern command puts the real distance at 23 kilometres and says staged flag-raisings feed Moscow's claims of capturing villages it still holds.

sections.text: Ukraine's Operation Task Force South said Russian commanders regularly report invented captures in Zaporizhzhia region and stage flag-raisings to create an illusion of advances [2]. Spokesperson Anastasiia Shevchenko said Valery Gerasimov told Russia's leadership last week that troops were five kilometres from Zaporizhzhia city, while Ukraine puts them 23 kilometres away, and that Vozdvyzhivka and Mala Tokmachka remain in Ukrainian hands [2]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the rebuttal comes from one Ukrainian military spokesperson and no independent mapping was checked this run.

items.title: Ukraine-Aligned ATESH Partisans Claim Sabotage Near a Moscow Data Centre
items.lede: The group says the aim is to blind Russian air defence crews before drone raids, but it offered no evidence of any outage at the site.

sections.text: The ATESH partisan movement said on Telegram that its agents in Russia were cutting military communication lines around the IXcellerate data centre in Moscow to help Ukrainian drones reach targets, Ukraine's Ukrinform reported [3]. ATESH alleged the Russian Defence Ministry hides command and air defence channels behind the commercial servers [3]. Ukrinform published the claim at 01:27 CEST on 22 October, during the overnight drone wave on the Moscow region. No evidence of damage and no Russian or company comment were found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low, because the claim comes only from the group itself, relayed by a Ukrainian state agency, with no independent sign of disruption.

items.title: Danish Police Charge Two Ukrainians with Spying on Counter-Drone Maker MyDefence
items.lede: The pair, aged 18 and 21, were caught filming facilities of a firm that supplies Ukraine, and denied the charges at a closed hearing in Aalborg.

sections.text: Police in North Jutland, Denmark, arrested two Ukrainian citizens on 19 October, working with the PET intelligence service, and an Aalborg court charged them with espionage the next day [4][5]. Public broadcaster DR reported that the target was MyDefence, a Danish maker of drone detection and jamming systems that supplies Ukraine's forces [4]. The suspects, aged 18 and 21, were charged under the criminal code's section on aiding a foreign intelligence service, denied the charges, and had their first hearing held behind closed doors [5]. PET warned that Russian services recruit people for simple photo tasks used to prepare sabotage against Danish defence firms [5]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the arrests and charges, because two secondary outlets cite the police and DR, but no police or PET release was read directly.

items.title: Bulgaria Shuts Burgas Port as Prosecutors Probe Drone Strike on Chelsea-3
items.lede: Bulgarian prosecutors ordered an explosives examination of debris from the ship, with results weeks away, as NATO patrol aircraft flew over the coast.

sections.text: After Romania shot down two Geran drones over its waters on 17 October, NATO said on 20 October allies were sending more maritime patrol aircraft, radars, explosive exploitation teams, and drones to the Black Sea [6][7][8]. On 21 October Bulgaria's Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov said Burgas port was closed for an investigation into debris tied to the drone strike on the Malta-flagged Chelsea-3, which was hit on 13 October about 17 nautical miles east of Byala [9][10][11]. The military prosecutor opened pre-trial proceedings; supervising prosecutor Kiril Peychinov said 11 to 15 surviving crew had been questioned, swabs taken, and the debris not yet confirmed as drone parts [11]. Stoyanov said a third Bulgarian surveillance drone system was flying over the sea and more military flights would follow [9][10]. No attribution of the attacks was announced, and Moscow denies involvement [8].

Confidence is high on the port closure and the investigation steps, because the minister and the prosecutor are quoted on record by three Bulgarian outlets. Confidence on the origin of the debris is low, because officials say it is unidentified.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: European Parliament Demands Faster Air Defences for Romania and Bulgaria
items.lede: Lawmakers voted 432 to 52 for an EU-NATO Black Sea task force and grain-route insurance, and faulted Sofia's weak response to recent Russian drone strikes.

sections.text: The European Parliament adopted a non-binding resolution on Thursday on escalating Russian strikes affecting the EU, particularly Black Sea shipping, by 432 votes to 52 with 88 abstentions, EU Perspectives reported [1]. It calls for faster delivery of air and sea defence systems to Romania, Bulgaria, and other coastal states, a top-up of the EU Solidarity Fund for damaged port cities, and Commission funding for alternative export routes and insurance guarantees for Ukrainian grain [1]. The joint text proposes an EU-NATO Black Sea maritime security task force and urges the Council to widen personal sanctions [1]. The Parliament said on X that it criticized the Bulgarian government's 'weak response' and called for better drone detection [1]. In Tuesday's debate, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas described six attacks by suspected Russian drones in ten days [1]. No Council response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the vote count and contents rest on one outlet's report, though it quotes the Parliament's own post.

items.title: France Jails 217 as Custody Cases From the Riots Reach 2,700
items.lede: The justice minister told prosecutors to seek voting-rights and social media bans for rioters, as Marseille's prosecutor said up to 3,000 people looted his city.

sections.text: France's Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said at Fleury-Mérogis prison on Thursday that 2,700 people had been held in custody since Saturday, more than 1,000 had been charged, and 217 were jailed, a figure 'still rising sharply' [2]. He said half had no criminal record and most were men aged 18 to 25 [2]. Darmanin instructed prosecutors to seek protest bans, temporary loss of civic rights including voting, and social media bans as added penalties [2]. Marseille prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said 1,800 to 3,000 people looted the city centre in 'concerted' attacks from 05:00 on 17 October, and that 34 of 50 people tried there were remanded [2]. Paris city hall counted 451 vandalized shops [2]. A second suspect in the arson at Limoges town hall was arrested with the RAID unit [2]. The police and gendarmerie inspectorates opened an inquiry after a minor was hurt in the eye in Dijon on Saturday, and a lawyer for the family of a 59-year-old man who died in Paris on 17 October plans a complaint [2].
Confidence is high on the custody and jail figures, because Darmanin and the Marseille prosecutor gave them on record. The detail rests on BFMTV's live report.

items.title: French Prefects Ban All Lyon Marches Saturday as Paris Approves a Union Route
items.lede: A court overturned a Thursday student-march ban in Paris, and police numbers for the weekend will rise by a fifth, with 20,000 or more counter-protesters expected in Orléans.

sections.text: The Rhône prefecture in France banned every protest in Lyon on 24 October, and Toulon barred marches in its centre from 11:00 to 23:59 [3][2]. In Paris, the police prefecture approved the CGT's Bastille-to-Nation route for Saturday and rejected a Bastille-to-Opéra route sought by the yellow vests, who said they would join the CGT march [2]. A Paris administrative court on Thursday suspended the ban on an Interfac student march, ordering the state to pay 1,000 euros; the prefecture then required it to stay static outside the Pitié-Salpêtrière hospital [2]. Junior interior minister Jean-Didier Berger said police numbers on Saturday would be 20 percent above 17 October, with leave cancelled and the GIGN and RAID units on call [2]. The Loiret prefect expects 20,000 to 30,000 opponents of the RN congress in Orléans on Saturday, including 2,000 to 3,000 radicals, and a source said Sunday protests there would be banned [2]. Government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon said bans would be decided case by case [2].
Confidence is high, because prefectures, the court, and ministers acted or spoke on record, reported by BFMTV and RTL. The Orléans Sunday ban rests on an unnamed source.

items.title: Italy Approves 175 Million Euros for Hauliers and Farmers as Southern Blockades Persist
items.lede: Prime Minister Meloni called the remaining roadblocks in Campania 'intimidation' and said police would use the law making road blocking a crime.

sections.text: Italy's cabinet on Thursday approved a decree with 175 million euros in aid: 105.2 million for road hauliers' diesel tax credits, 60 million for farm fuel, and 10 million for fishing [4]. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said Transport Minister Matteo Salvini had signed an agreement with hauliers' associations and that payments had begun [4]. She said 'a few' people were still blocking roads, threatening drivers and slashing tyres, called it 'intimidation', and said the government would use the security decree that made road blocking a crime [4]. Deputy minister Edoardo Rixi said the first 2,000 firms would receive their credits next week; hauliers have until 31 March 2027 to use the credits, and further measures requested by their associations, such as deferring leasing payments, are planned [4]. Earlier, the Interior Ministry said 1,339 people had been identified and 71 reported [5]. Blockades were lifted in Sicily and Calabria, but disruption continued on Campania's motorways and fishing boats stayed in port [4]. Justice Minister Carlo Nordio said mafia infiltration of the protests was 'highly probable' [4].
Confidence is high, because the decree and Meloni's and ministers' statements are on record in ANSA. Nordio's view is his own assessment.

items.title: Macron Orders Bans on Protests 'Without Legitimacy' After French Security Council
items.lede: He blamed organised ultra-left groups for 'seditious' violence, admitted intelligence failures, and called a defence council for Friday.

sections.text: President Emmanuel Macron said after an Élysée meeting with France's intelligence chiefs on Thursday that prefects would ban protests called by groups 'with no legitimacy', and offer unions alternative routes to protect city centres, shops, and public buildings [6][2]. The Élysée said the council, with Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and the ministers concerned, reviewed 'the dysfunctions' behind last weekend's events [7]. Macron admitted 'failures of anticipation' and called last Saturday's violence 'seditious' acts by organised ultra-left groups seeking to 'bring down the Republic', alongside ordinary crime [6][8]. He will chair a defence council on Friday, promising 'additional decisions', and visit police and gendarmes [6][2]. Lecornu will meet student, union, employer, and local-government groups on Monday [6]. At Matignon on Thursday afternoon, Lecornu received party leaders with Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez and Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin [2]. Bruno Retailleau left early and again demanded a state of emergency, while the Socialists' Olivier Faure and the Ecologists' Marine Tondelier accused the government of a purely security-based response [2].
Confidence is high, because Macron spoke on camera, the Élysée issued a communiqué, and Reuters, BFMTV, and Europe 1 agree.

items.title: Lyon Renews Its Curfew for a Fourth Night Ahead of Saturday Protests
items.lede: The Rhône prefect also banned protest gatherings in the Presqu'île from 16:00 to 23:00, after officials described the earlier curfew nights as calm.

sections.text: The Rhône prefecture in France renewed the curfew in central Lyon for the night of 22 to 23 October from 23:00 to 06:00, with a ban on all protest marches and gatherings in the same part of the Presqu'île from 16:00 to 23:00 [2]. On the night of 21 to 22 October, Paris barred everyone from parts of the city, including Place de la République, from 23:00 to 06:00 for a third night, and Lyon's curfew ran from 23:00 [9][10]. The Nord prefect extended minors-only curfews in Lille, Douai, Denain, and Wattignies from 20:00 to 06:00 until Friday morning [11][10]. Marseille's minors-only curfew covered the city centre and several shopping centres [9]. Toulon will impose a minors' curfew from 18:00 on Saturday [2]. No police report of disorder during the curfews was found by the cutoff, and no Paris renewal for Thursday night was found.
Confidence on the orders is high, because the prefectures issued them and BFMTV, franceinfo, RFI, and Le Figaro report them.

items.title: UK Lawmakers Warn of 'Glaring Gaps' in Britain's Arctic Defences Against Russia
items.lede: The Commons Defence Committee cited too few warships, low submarine availability, and a lost ability to operate under ice, while the defence ministry pointed to new investment.

sections.text: The UK House of Commons Defence Committee said in a report published on Thursday that Britain has 'glaring gaps' in its ability to defend the High North, leaving undersea cables, energy supplies, and the nuclear deterrent exposed to Russia [12][13]. It said the Royal Navy has five Type 23 frigates and six Type 45 destroyers, just over half its requirement of 19, and found 'shockingly low availability' of submarines and a temporary loss of the ability to operate them beneath Arctic ice [13][12]. Chairman Tan Dhesi said work on the gaps 'cannot start soon enough' if Russia could attack NATO by 2030 [12][13]. The committee asked whether the UK-led Joint Expeditionary Force should focus more on the High North, and Dhesi said Britain might need to reinforce its army presence in Estonia to offset that [13]. The Ministry of Defence said it was 'clear-eyed' about the threat and cited £1.5 billion for its Atlantic Bastion programme and £330 million for undersea infrastructure [13][12]. The report came days after HMS Prince of Wales left Portsmouth on Sunday for an Arctic and North Atlantic deployment [13].
Confidence is high, because the committee and the ministry spoke on record and the BBC and The Independent agree. The fleet figures are the committee's.

items.title: Portuguese Protesters Strike Rossio Tents but Vote to Sleep in the Square
items.lede: A Lisbon assembly backed the open-air option with 338 votes after police set a deadline, and the movement has called a Saturday march and urged a general strike.

sections.text: Protesters in Lisbon, Portugal, voted at an assembly early on Thursday to take down their tents in Rossio square and sleep in the open, after the PSP police warned that gatherings in public places were not permitted and set 00:30 Lisbon time as the deadline for removing the tents, RTP reported [14]. The option won 338 votes, ahead of leaving or keeping the tents behind a human cordon [14]. Earlier on Wednesday night, an assembly had voted to camp again but not to resist removal, Expresso reported [15]. Interior Minister Luís Neves had said the PSP would act 'pre-emptively' and not allow tents [16][14]. The 55 people detained on Tuesday will be heard on 27 October [15][17]. The movement called a march from Marquês de Pombal to Rossio at 15:00 on Saturday and urged a general strike [15]. Near 22:00, PSP officers escorted a man waving an Israeli flag into the metro after protesters pushed him out [15]. No police removal of the camp was found by the cutoff.
Confidence on the overnight vote is moderate, because it rests on RTP's live report. Confidence on the earlier vote, the detentions, and the hearing date is high.

items.title: EU Agencies Urge Rapid PHP Fixes as European Governments Take Websites Offline
items.lede: The Netherlands, France, Belgium, Finland, and the Czech Republic shut state sites as a precaution, and Dutch and US cyber agencies said they had seen no active exploitation.

sections.text: The European Commission, the EU cyber agency ENISA, CERT-EU, Europol, and the EU's national response teams said on Wednesday that two critical flaws in PHP, a language widely used for websites, could let attackers run code remotely without authentication, and urged organisations to apply the fixes released at 15:40 CEST or isolate exposed systems [18]. In the Netherlands, the national cyber centre advised site owners to consider going offline, and Overheid.nl, MijnOverheid, and DigiD were pulled [19]. MijnOverheid and DigiD were back by evening, but Overheid.nl was still down at 22:54 [20][21]. France's Interior Ministry took prefecture websites offline, and Belgium's foreign ministry did the same, though Belgium's cyber centre recorded no attacks on Belgian sites [22]. Finland's state IT centre shut public government web services, and the Czech government took its site down at 19:00 [22]. NOS reported Belgian and French government sites still unavailable late on Wednesday [21]. Cloudflare's technology chief said early attacks were emerging [23].
Confidence is high, because the EU bodies and the Dutch government stated it on record and Reuters, NOS, and CNBC agree. The scale of any exploitation is unclear.

items.title: Spain's Constitutional Court Leaves About 163,000 New Citizens' Votes in Doubt
items.lede: Judges voted 10 to 2 that the ombudsman's appeal was premature, sending the suspension of voting rights under the 'grandchildren's law' back to the Supreme Court.

sections.text: Spain's Constitutional Court on Wednesday rejected, by 10 votes to 2, an appeal by ombudsman Ángel Gabilondo against the Supreme Court's provisional suspension of voting rights for people naturalized under the Democratic Memory Law [24][25]. The majority found the appeal premature because the Supreme Court is still taking submissions from those affected, and two progressive judges, Juan Carlos Campo and Ramón Sáez, dissented [24][25]. The Supreme Court's suspension covers 163,020 people, according to government figures cited in its orders, who cannot vote in the 29 November general election unless consulates certify that they descend from exiles [25]. Gabilondo said he respected the decision but was concerned that citizens would lose a fundamental right [25]. The government said the ruling was procedural, did not address the merits, and that 'all Spanish nationals have the right to vote' [24][25]. Vox, which had asked the Constitutional Court to reject the appeal, was among those that brought the original Supreme Court challenge [25][24].

Confidence is high, because the Constitutional Court's decision and the government's and ombudsman's responses are on record and El País and RTVE agree. The 163,020 figure rests on RTVE's report of the Supreme Court's orders; El País gives a round 160,000.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Lithuania Finds About 100 Websites Exposed to Critical PHP Flaw
items.lede: The cyber agency rates the threat 9.5 out of 10 but has seen no attacks yet, while the state registry briefly suspended services.

sections.text: Around 100 websites in Lithuania, run by both private firms and state institutions, are vulnerable to a critical PHP flaw, National Cyber Security Centre head Antanas Aleknavičius told M1 radio on 22 October, BNS reported via LRT [1]. The centre rated the threat 9.5 out of 10, warned institutions on 21 October, and is running further scans [1]. The Centre of Registers temporarily suspended some services and said on 22 October they were being restored [1]. Aleknavičius said exploit tools are being developed but there is no evidence yet they have been used [1].
Confidence is moderate, because one public broadcaster relays the agency head's on-record remarks; no centre release was read.

items.title: Estonia Takes Delivery of 70-km HIMARS Rockets as ATACMS Stay on Hold
items.lede: Defence Minister Martin Herem says the 300-km missiles remain held up by the US pause, and Korean Chunmoo munitions may slip to 2028.

sections.text: Estonian Defence Minister Martin Herem confirmed to ERR on 22 October that GMLRS rockets with a range of about 70 km for Estonia's HIMARS launchers have arrived [2]. Estonia also ordered ATACMS missiles with a range of up to 300 km, but the United States suspended ammunition deliveries in the spring because of the war in Iraq, and the long-range missiles remain on hold [2]. Herem said launchers for South Korea's Chunmoo system arrive next year, with their ammunition more likely in early 2028 [2].
Confidence is moderate, because one public broadcaster reports the minister's on-record remarks; no US statement was read.

items.title: EU Grants Estonia €32 Million for Drone Surveillance on Eastern Border
items.lede: The interior minister also says illegal transits from Belarus via Latvia have jumped tenfold, to 406 this year against 39 last year.

sections.text: Estonian Interior Minister Igor Taro said at the government's weekly press conference on 22 October that the European Union will give Estonia €32 million to strengthen drone surveillance along the eastern border, compared with €4 million budgeted for other border infrastructure next year [3]. Taro also said 406 people had been apprehended in Estonia by 20 October for illegally transiting after crossing the Latvia–Belarus border, against 39 in all of last year [3].
Confidence is moderate, because one public broadcaster reports the minister's on-record remarks; no Commission notice was read.

items.title: Latvian Military Declares Possible Air Threat over Two Eastern Districts
items.lede: Residents near the Russian and Belarusian borders got phone alerts telling them no action was needed, and the warning lifted after 37 minutes.

sections.text: Latvia's National Armed Forces declared a possible threat to Latvian airspace over the Krāslava and Rēzekne districts in the east of the country at 12:39 on 22 October and cancelled it at 13:16, LSM reported [4]. Phone alerts told residents that no further action was required [4]. The cause was not stated, and no drone sighting or interception was reported by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one public broadcaster relays the military's notice; the cause is unknown.

items.title: Smuggling Balloons Explode on Power Lines in Central Lithuania
items.lede: Firefighters found burning balloon fragments in two districts, at dawn and late at night, as the cigarette-smuggling flights keep reaching inland villages.

sections.text: Two balloons carrying smuggled cigarettes exploded after striking power lines in central Lithuania on 21 October, the Kaunas Fire and Rescue Service said on 22 October, BNS reported via LRT [5]. The first hit lines in Padotnuvys village, Kėdainiai district, at about 06:00, and the second burned in a field in Šakniai village, Kaišiadorys district, at about 23:00 [5]. No injuries or outages were reported in the article [5].
Confidence is moderate, because one public broadcaster relays the fire service's account.

items.title: Lithuania Seeks Iranian Confirmation That Two Women Are Detained
items.lede: Vilnius has drafted a diplomatic note, and police opened a search after relatives lost contact with the tourists on 11 October.

sections.text: Lithuania's Foreign Ministry is seeking official confirmation of reports that two Lithuanian women have been detained in Iran, a senior ministry official told LRT on 22 October [6]. The ministry has prepared a diplomatic note, and the honorary consul is also seeking confirmation; the reasons are unknown [6]. Police say the women flew from Turkey to Iran after leaving Lithuania on 7 October, and relatives lost contact on 11 October [6]. No Iranian statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the search and the ministry's steps, because one public broadcaster reports them; the detention itself is unconfirmed.

items.title: Bundeswehr Rehearses Rushing Reinforcements into Estonia for First Time
items.lede: Convoys of Germany's 4th Logistics Regiment have moved by ferry, road, and air during a 10-day drill, though troop numbers stay undisclosed.

sections.text: Germany's 4th Logistics Regiment is practising, for the first time in Estonia, the deployment of extra troops during the 10-day Brave Blue 26 exercise running 16–27 October, ERR reported on 22 October [7]. Convoys have been visible since 16 October, and regiment commander Lieutenant Colonel Benjamin Eberhardt said equipment came by ferry and soldiers by plane [7]. The drill rehearses reinforcing German units in the Baltic states in a crisis; similar exercises were held earlier in Lithuania and Latvia [7]. Germany did not disclose troop or vehicle numbers [7].
Confidence is moderate, because one public broadcaster reports the exercise and the commander's remarks; no Bundeswehr release was read.

items.title: Latvia Pulls 165 State Websites Offline over Critical PHP Flaws
items.lede: The cyber agency says about 95% of key state systems are patched and reachable from Latvia with no successful attacks, though foreign access stays blocked and some portals remain down.

sections.text: Latvian authorities suspended access on 21 October to the shared government web platform hosting 165 state and municipal sites after two critical vulnerabilities were found in the PHP programming language, Rīga TV reported [8]. Public broadcaster LSM and Latvian Radio also took their sites and app offline as a precaution [9]. Access from inside Latvia was restored shortly after 22:00 local time, while access from abroad stayed restricted; the official gazette and Likumi.lv legal portal were still down later [8]. CERT.lv deputy head Varis Teivāns said bots were attempting attacks but none on key state resources had succeeded, and fewer than 20 important resources remained fully inaccessible [10]. By Thursday afternoon CERT.lv said about 95% of important state resources were updated and available from Latvia; the official gazette was partly back, while Likumi.lv and Latvian Radio's website remained offline [11][12].
Confidence is high, because three outlets report the shutdown and officials' statements consistently; the CERT.lv notice itself was not read.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Serbia's Campaign Closes with Rallies as Student List Challenges Vučić
items.lede: Watchdogs report threats and violence during the race, and European observers will monitor Sunday's vote among about 6.5 million voters.

sections.text: Rallies took place across Serbia on 22 October, the final day of campaigning before the 25 October snap parliamentary election, BBC News reported [1]. About 6.5 million voters choose between Aleksandar Vučić's SNS-led 'United Serbia' list and the student-led 'Student List', whose lead candidate is cardiologist Ilija Srdanović [2] [1]. European observers will monitor the vote; PACE has described a 'tense and divisive electoral climate', and watchdog CRTA has warned of threats and physical violence [1]. The Guardian notes media bias, intimidation, and voter-list irregularities mean any result could be contested [2].
Confidence is high, because BBC News and the Guardian report the campaign close and the main contenders consistently.

items.title: Merz Urges Kosovo and Serbia to Revive Dialogue at Montenegro Summit
items.lede: Kosovo's Albin Kurti pressed for an account of more than 1,500 missing persons as Montenegro closed its term chairing the Berlin Process.

sections.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for immediate progress in the Kosovo–Serbia dialogue at the Berlin Process leaders' summit in Miločer, near Budva, Montenegro, on 22 October, Albeu reported [3]; Montenegrin Prime Minister Milojko Spajić opened the summit that morning [4]. Merz urged Pristina and Belgrade to avoid escalation and rhetoric that fuels conflict, saying 'we must not pour gasoline on the fire' [3]. Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti demanded justice for war crimes, an account of more than 1,500 missing persons, and cited 23 Albanian bodies recently exhumed in Zubin Potok [3]. The summit ends Montenegro's chairmanship of the process [3]. North Macedonia's Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski said he expected strong messages on EU integration, as his country's accession talks have still not begun [5].
Confidence is moderate, because one regional outlet reports the remarks; no German government transcript was read.

items.title: Croatia's Plenković Welcomes Montenegro's Steps on Kotor Pool and Morinj Plaque
items.lede: Zagreb's prime minister plans talks with his Montenegrin counterpart after the summit, a sign that a bilateral row is easing.

sections.text: Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković said on 22 October, ahead of the Berlin Process summit in Montenegro, that he would meet Montenegrin Prime Minister Milojko Spajić afterwards to discuss outstanding bilateral issues, CdM reported [6]. Plenković welcomed Montenegro's decisions to rename a swimming pool in Kotor and legally formalise a memorial plaque at the former Morinj camp, calling both steps in the right direction [6]. No readout of the meeting was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one Montenegrin outlet reports the on-record remarks.

items.title: Albania's Medical Students Join Tenth Day of Protests Against Rama
items.lede: Protesters again refused talks with the prime minister and toppled his 'dialogue' blocks, a day after Molotov cocktails hit police lines.

sections.text: On 22 October, the tenth straight day of protests in Tirana, Albania, students and professors rallied outside parliament, joined by students of the University of Medicine, while socialist MPs pushed through fast-tracked bills amid clashes with opposition MPs inside [7]. Protesters then moved to the prime minister's office, rejected Prime Minister Edi Rama's renewed offer of dialogue, and overturned concrete blocks marked 'dialogue' [8]. On the evening of 21 October masked groups threw Molotov cocktails, stones, and fireworks at police outside the prime minister's office, and police answered with water cannon and tear gas [9] [10]. State Police earlier reported 271 arrests over seven days, and health data put injuries at 320 [11] [12] [13]. No police toll for 21 or 22 October was read by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the 21 October clashes and earlier counts, because RTSH, Periskopi, police, and health figures agree; confidence is moderate on 22 October, because two private outlets report it.

items.title: Serbian Police Detain Seven over Alleged Election-Day Violence Plot
items.lede: Prosecutors call it a plan to topple the state, while opposition figures say raids on Student List supporters found only campaign leaflets.

sections.text: Serbian police arrested five people aged 27 and 28 in Novi Sad on 21 October, and Belgrade prosecutors said they planned violence, riots, and attacks on opponents and police on the 25 October election day, Balkan Insight and BBC Serbian reported [14] [15]. Prosecutors said the group planned mobile teams with balaclavas, poles, flares, knives, and weapons to travel to Belgrade, and one suspect was to command about 40 people [14] [15]. A Belgrade activist of the group Belgrade Stays and a Student List supporter in Vrnjačka Banja were also detained; their lawyer and a local coordinator said searches found nothing but campaign material [14] [15]. All face up to 48 hours' detention [14].
Confidence is high on the arrests, because two independent outlets report them and the prosecutor's statement; the plot allegations rest on prosecutors alone and are untested.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the South Caucasus

items.title: Pashinyan Accuses Circles in Russia and Armenia of Targeting Independence
items.lede: The prime minister says Moscow's curbs on Armenian goods since April have failed, calling it the third destabilisation attempt in three years.

sections.text: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on 22 October that 'circles' in Russia and Armenia seek to destabilise the country with the aim of eliminating Armenia's de facto independence, OC Media reported [1]. He said Russian restrictions on Armenian goods since April had failed to produce the intended economic and political effects, and called the effort the third such attempt in three years [1]. No Kremlin response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet reports the on-record remarks; the government transcript was not read.

items.title: Georgia's Constitutional Court Rejects Opposition Motions in Party-Ban Hearing
items.lede: Judges turned down bids to involve Strasbourg and Venice Commission experts, and the speaker called Western criticism interference before the third hearing day.

sections.text: On 22 October, the second day of hearings in Batumi, Georgia, on Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban five opposition parties, the Constitutional Court rejected Lelo/Strong Georgia's motion to seek an advisory opinion from the European Court of Human Rights, Civil.ge reported [2]. Judge Revaz Nadaraia said the motion reflected 'lack of trust' in the court [2]. The court also refused to summon three Venice Commission experts online [2]. Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili called foreign criticism of the case an attempt to pressure the court [2]. Hearings continue on 23 October [2].
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet's live coverage reports the rulings; the court's own record was not read.

items.title: Freedom House Downgrades Georgia's Internet Freedom to Partly Free
items.lede: The watchdog cut the score two points to 68, citing retaliation against online journalists and social media users critical of the ruling party.

sections.text: Georgia's status fell from 'Free' to 'Partly Free' in Freedom House's 2026 Freedom on the Net report, with its score down from 70 to 68 out of 100, Civil.ge reported on 22 October [3]. The watchdog cited an 'extended crackdown' by Georgian Dream authorities on online activism and retaliation against critical journalists and social media users, covering June 2025 to May 2026 [3]. No government response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet reports the findings; the report itself was not read.

items.title: Azerbaijani Police Reportedly Detain 88 in Nardaran over Hijab Protests
items.lede: An activist says most face criminal charges and lack independent lawyers, while the official count stood at 37 detentions and six student arrests.

sections.text: Reports say 88 people have been detained in Azerbaijan's Nardaran village during protests against hijab restrictions in schools, OC Media reported on 22 October, citing activist Alamdar Bunyatov [4]. Authorities earlier said 37 were detained and six students arrested over an alleged attempt to burn a school [4]. Bunyatov said most detainees face criminal charges, four were remanded for three months, and families were denied independent lawyers [4]. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan phoned President Ilham Aliyev on 21 October; the readout did not mention the protests [4].
Confidence is moderate on official figures and low on the 88 count, because it rests on one activist via one outlet.

items.title: Moscow Denies Political Motive in Curbs on Georgian Drinks
items.lede: Russia's foreign ministry spokeswoman blames the consumer watchdog, while Georgian producers reject quality complaints that echo the 2006 wine ban.

sections.text: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said on 21 October that new restrictions on some Georgian beverages are targeted quality-control measures by consumer watchdog Rospotrebnadzor, not politically motivated, OC Media reported [5]. Georgian companies have rejected claims their products fail standards [5]. Russia banned Georgian wine in 2006 and later restricted Borjomi and Nabeghlavi mineral water [5].
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet reports the briefing; the ministry transcript was not read.

items.title: Armenia to Return Azerbaijani Shepherd Who Crossed into Tavush
items.lede: Security officials say the man got lost, and the prime minister confirmed the handover in the second such crossing in recent weeks.

sections.text: Armenia's National Security Service said Azerbaijani citizen Yashar Kasimov, born in 1968, from Tovuz district, was found in Armenia's Tavush province on 19 October after getting lost, and that steps are being taken to return him, OC Media reported [6]. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan confirmed on 22 October that he will be handed back [6]. It was the second such crossing in recent weeks, and authorities disclosed it only after media reports [6].
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet reports the NSS statement and Pashinyan's remarks.

items.title: Georgian Prosecutors Charge Journalist Chubinidze with Treason over Gareji Claims
items.lede: Prosecutors say his reporting that the prime minister ceded parts of a historic monastery to Azerbaijan amounts to sabotage carrying up to four years.

sections.text: Georgia's Prosecutor's Office arrested Dito Chubinidze, a journalist with the weekly Asaval-Dasavali, and said on 22 October he will be charged with high treason, 'particularly sabotage', facing up to four years in prison, Civil.ge reported [7] [8]. Prosecutors accuse him of deliberately spreading false reports that Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze handed parts of the Davit Gareji monastery complex to Azerbaijan [7]. The case follows allegations by jailed former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, including over the death of commentator Lazare Jorbenadze, who made similar claims in interviews with Chubinidze [7]. Prosecutors said their inquiry found no agreement with Azerbaijan on the border at Davit Gareji [8].
Confidence is high on the arrest and charge, because Civil.ge and OC Media report the prosecutors' announcement.

theaters.heading: Politics, the Bundeswehr, the economy, and developments in Baden-Württemberg

items.title: Klingbeil's Tax Estimate Finds Extra Revenue but No New Room in Germany's Budget
items.lede: Higher growth tightens Germany's debt-brake borrowing limit, so the CDU/CSU's hoped-for electricity-tax cut is unlikely to be funded from the windfall.

sections.text: Germany's official tax estimators now expect €10.9 billion more revenue across all levels of government in 2027 than forecast in May, including €4.1 billion more for the federal government, Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) said in Berlin on Thursday [1] [2]. Federal tax revenue for 2027 is put at €398.6 billion, and the cumulative gain through 2030 at €43.4 billion [1]. Because the economy is improving, the debt brake's cyclical component lets the government borrow less than planned, which absorbs much of the gain; Klingbeil said 2027 brings no new room but also no new gaps, and consolidation is still needed [1]. dpa reported that the gain alone is unlikely to fund an electricity-tax cut sought by the CDU/CSU [1].
Confidence is high on the figures and the minister's statements, because dpa and ZDF report them from his presentation. The estimate document itself was not read.

items.title: German Prosecutors Arrest Ukrainian Suspected of Spying for Russian Intelligence
items.lede: The suspect allegedly mined contacts in Europe's arms industry for data on tank and ammunition output, and Chancellor Merz warned such cases will multiply.

sections.text: Germany's Federal Prosecutor had federal police (BKA) arrest Ukrainian national Vadym Y. in the Oder-Spree district of Brandenburg on Thursday on a warrant issued 15 October [3] [4]. Prosecutors say he was in contact with a Russian intelligence service through an intermediary since at least July 2025 and gathered information on production of armoured vehicles, ammunition, and explosives, and on personnel and military sites securing NATO's eastern flank [3]. Some of it was public; for the rest he allegedly pumped contacts in the European defence industry [3]. The case began with a tip from the domestic intelligence service, and he is due before a Federal Court of Justice judge on Friday [3] [5]. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Russian intelligence activity in Germany remains 'unchanged high' and such cases will likely become more frequent [5]. No comment from Kyiv or Moscow was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the arrest and the allegations, because they come from the prosecutor's own statement and are reported by the Stuttgarter Zeitung and by Al Jazeera citing AFP and Reuters. The allegations are unproven and no charge has been filed.

items.title: Many Baden-Württemberg City Websites Stay Dark After PHP Flaw Shutdown
items.lede: State ministries in Germany's southwest are largely back online, but municipal and some university sites await patches with no restoration date given.

sections.text: Websites of Baden-Württemberg's ministries and regional councils had been unreachable for several hours on Wednesday afternoon; the State Ministry told dpa this was a precaution until developers ship security updates, after which the sites return [6]. University and hospital sites in Freiburg, Heidelberg, Mannheim, Tübingen, and Ulm, plus KIT in Karlsruhe and DHBW Mosbach, were also taken down; the Heidelberg and Mannheim university hospitals said this was not a cyberattack and patient care was unaffected [7] [8] [6]. The federal cyber agency BSI warned that all known PHP versions back to PHP 5 may let attackers run code remotely, said patches were due at 16:00, and called large-scale exploitation within hours of release likely [9]. Ulm and Tübingen universities restored their sites on Wednesday evening [10]. By Thursday morning the ministries' homepages were largely reachable again, but sites of many larger cities and of Heidelberg and Konstanz universities were still offline, with no date for full restoration [11]. The BSI rates the two vulnerabilities, dubbed 'PHP2Shell', at warning level 3 of 4, 'orange' [12].
Confidence is high on the shutdowns and their precautionary nature, because the State Ministry, the hospitals, SWR, and the Stuttgarter Zeitung agree, and the BSI confirms the flaw.

items.title: Bayaz Tables €72 Billion 2027 Budget for Baden-Württemberg, Germany
items.lede: Cities say the extra billion falls short, with nine in ten unable to balance their books, while the minister warns the state's reserves are nearly exhausted.

sections.text: Baden-Württemberg Finance Minister Danyal Bayaz (Greens) introduced the 2027 state budget of €72 billion in the Landtag on Wednesday, with a final vote due after debate in December [13]. The plan gives municipalities more than €1 billion extra, adds 650 police posts and 3,400 school posts, and cuts 550 administrative posts this term [13]. Bayaz said buffers are largely used up and room for manoeuvre is tight [13]. Ralf Broß of the state association of cities said over 90 percent of municipalities cannot present a balanced budget after a €4.4 billion deficit last year [13]. Opposition reaction was not found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the figures come from one SWR report quoting the minister and the cities' association on record, and the budget documents were not read.

items.title: Germany Counts About 20 Far-Right 'Active Clubs' as Fight Groups Spread
items.lede: The Interior Ministry warns that combat training is making the groups more capable of violence, though it has recorded no direct attacks on opponents yet.

sections.text: Germany's federal government knows of about 20 regional far-right 'Active Clubs', up from 'about a dozen' in June 2024, according to the Interior Ministry's answer to a Green Party inquiry reported by RND and dpa [14] [15]. The ministry said the rise was especially marked during 2026 and that regular combat training and martial videos point to a 'professionalisation of violence skills' [14] [15]. It found no direct clashes with political opponents so far and no known links to foreign Active Clubs, while noting strong recruitment of young men [14]. The concept comes from the United States [15]. Green MP Marlene Schönberger told RND the government has no figures on offences or known dangerous persons in the groups and wants the issue on the interior ministers' December agenda [14].

Confidence is high on the government's figures, because Deutschlandfunk and the Stuttgarter Zeitung both report the ministry's written answer. Both rest on the same RND and dpa reporting, and the answer itself was not read.

items.title: Berlin Steps Up Monitoring Before Germany's 31 October 'Gen Z' Protests
items.lede: Federal police may turn back people entering Germany to join violent riots, while organisers reported more than 10,000 sign-ups by Wednesday and insist they reject violence.

sections.text: The initiative 'Gen Z steht auf' has called rallies in 22 German cities on 31 October, according to its website [16], including Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Karlsruhe, and Freiburg, demanding better education, affordable living, and no conscription [17] [18]. Co-initiator Akram Selo said the group rejects all violence [17] [18]. Baden-Württemberg Interior Minister Manuel Hagel told the Landtag on Wednesday that police are preparing intensively and would respond 'with the full force of the rule of law'; Bavaria's Joachim Herrmann also issued a warning [17]. Hesse's Roman Poseck said left-wing groups are using the mobilisation and promised a strong police presence; Frankfurt has a registered demo with 1,700 expected [18] [19]. On Wednesday evening a federal Interior Ministry spokesman said federal and state agencies are coordinating in the joint counter-extremism centre, with threat assessments shared with France and Italy [20]. He said domestic intelligence is stepping up monitoring of websites and social media, and that federal police may turn back people trying to enter Germany to join violent riots [20]. The organisers' website listed more than 10,000 registrations on Wednesday evening [20].

Confidence is high on the call to protest and the officials' statements, because dpa, hr, tagesschau, and the Stuttgarter Zeitung quote them on record. The registration figure comes from the organisers' website.
